thread:
incident-bot: Pager: P1 - regional DNS/resolver mismatch in EU (eu-west-2), rule=geo-dns-healthcheck-flap. https://infra.redwood/alerts/67890
maya_oncall: I'm the oncall, taking lead. @rafael_netops @sam_sre please confirm. Any user-facing symptoms?
rafael_netops: Synthetic monitoring shows routing flips between eu-west-2a ELB IPs and an old replica set in eu-west-2b. Route53 Latency/Failover policy is toggling because our ALB health checks are flapping in 2a. Some public resolvers (notably ISP resolvers in EU) are returning stale CNAME glue which points to the retired elb hostname.
sam_sre: Observed application 502/504s for EU customers starting ~2060007700. Probes: dig reveals two different CNAME chains depending on resolver — one points to albs/active.elb.amazonaws.com, another to retired-alb.old.aws. Example:
```
$ dig +short www.redwood-eu.example.com @1.1.1.1
retired-alb.old.aws
$ dig +short www.redwood-eu.example.com @8.8.8.8
active-alb.elb.amazonaws.com
```
maya_oncall: That explains split behavior. Immediate mitigations?
rafael_netops: Options: 1) Pause health checks on the failing ALB to stop Route53 failover churn, 2) Upsert parent-zone A records for critical endpoints to authoritative IPs in healthy AZs, 3) Force Route53 to route-weight to healthy set, 4) Contact Cloudflare to purge resolver-side caches if they are returning stale glue.
sam_sre: I'm for (1)+(2) to stop the oscillation fast. I'll pause the ALB health checks and reduce Route53 TTLs to 30s to accelerate the change. Also will prepare the temp A upsert for api and www.
maya_oncall: Do it, and tell support to post a status update.
support_lead: Support queue shows ~40 incoming EU tickets, mostly timeouts/502, some API customers hitting increased error budgets. Posting status.redwood.com: "Intermittent EU routing/DNS issues, mitigation in progress." Link: https://status.redwood.com/incident/2060007777
rafael_netops: Executing commands now:
aws elbv2 modify-target-group-attributes --target-group-arn arn:aws:... --attributes Key=health.check.enabled,Value=false
aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id ZEU1 --change-batch '{"Changes":[{"Action":"UPSERT","ResourceRecordSet":{"Name":"www.redwood-eu.example.com","Type":"A","TTL":30,"ResourceRecords":[{"Value":"3.102.45.11"},{"Value":"3.102.45.12"}]}}]}'
Change submitted CHNG-206A1. Disabling health checks should stop ELB-level flapping in a couple of seconds.
sam_sre: After change CHNG-206A1 propagated, synthetic error rate dropped from 22% -> 6% in 4 minutes. Some resolvers still resolve to retired host for non-critical subdomains due to TTL and glue caching.
maya_oncall: Good progress. Open vendor ticket with Cloudflare and mention retired-alb host in responses. We need to know if their resolvers cached the retired host's NS/glue longer than TTL.
cloudflare_support_bot: Ticket CF-100123 opened, escalated to infra ops. Attach probe logs, dig samples, and change IDs CHNG-206A1.
support_lead: CSM outreach: @csm_nora please prepare messages to top EU customers and offer immediate traffic migration to Dedicated if they have strict SLAs.
csm_nora: Drafting message now, pushing to customers with highest error volumes.
rafael_netops: Plan for cleanup: 1) re-enable health checks with corrected target registration after we confirm no instance drift; 2) raise TTLs back to normal (300) after 30m; 3) retire temp A records once resolver population stabilizes.
maya_oncall: Note runbook: add a step to check ALB target registration and remove retired CNAMES from origin config to prevent recurrence. Also add synthetic probes that include ISP resolvers and Cloudflare/Google/Quad9.
sam_sre: I'll document exact commands and timestamps for the postmortem. Quick timeline for notes:
- 2060007700: First synthetic alerts (EU) - 502/504 increase
- 2060007725: Dig traces show mixed CNAME answers across resolvers
- 2060007740: Oncall engaged and health checks paused
- 2060007755: Route53 temp A upsert CHNG-206A1 submitted
- 2060007800: Error rates drop; support queue stabilizes
- 2060007820: Cloudflare ticket CF-100123 opened and acknowledged
maya_oncall: Incident to P2 (partial degradation contained) at 2060007900. Keep monitoring for 60m. Assign action items: rafael_netops (investigate cause of health-check flapping + remove retired CNAMES), sam_sre (postmortem + add resolver diversity probes), csm_nora (customer outreach follow-ups).
support_lead: Status page updated with mitigation and ETA for full resolution. No major enterprise SLA breaches reported yet; standing by for any escalations.
cloudflare_support_bot: CF interim update: internal purge running, caches expected to expire within 15-45 minutes depending on resolver. They requested TTL/NS history which we provided.
rafael_netops: Follow-up: found that a deployment rollback last week left a legacy CNAME in origin config which registered the retired ALB as a potential backend; that caused occasional health-check failures and some resolvers learned the retired CNAME. Will remove legacy config and submit RFC for NS hygiene.
maya_oncall: Great. Incident closed to monitoring at 2060008042. Classification: internal config + health-check churn leading to DNS split-brain across resolvers; mitigated with health-check pause, parent-level A upsert, vendor cache purge. Action items assigned and postmortem scheduled.
